label: Outerwear — jackets, coats, blazers
note: Authored, never generated. Outerwear needs two states: the hero is fastened (the intended silhouette), and the open state is a normal fan-out FROM that hero — modelling it as a second step-1 hero would generate a second person. The lining macro is optional and gated on an 'inside' reference: most brands won't supply one, and without gating the model would invent a lining.
preserve_fields: the shell fabric colour, texture and sheen
the collar or lapel shape and how it rolls
the closure — its type, count, spacing and hardware finish
the pocket type, placement and any flaps or welts
the shoulder line, sleeve head and cuff construction
the body length, hem finish and any vent or belt

ref_descriptions.front: the front of a jacket photographed flat on a headless mannequin
ref_descriptions.back: the BACK of the same jacket photographed on a mannequin
ref_descriptions.detail: a macro of the same jacket's closure, collar and fabric
ref_descriptions.inside: the INSIDE of the same jacket showing its lining

blocks.keep_onmodel: Keep the SAME {{campaign.pronoun.noun}} (identical face, hair, skin tone and build), the SAME {{product.short_name}} with its shell fabric, collar, closure and pockets unchanged, the SAME {{wardrobe_short}}, and the SAME {{campaign.set_short}} and {{campaign.light_short}}.
blocks.must_preserve: MUST PRESERVE EXACTLY from the references, unchanged: {{product.garment}}; and {{preserve_fields}}. Do not redraw, restyle, recolour, resize or reposition the closure, collar, pockets or hardware. Do not add any extra text, logo or graphic anywhere on the garment.
blocks.tail: {{campaign.grade}}, sharp focus, no motion blur, no extra text or logos.
blocks.no_person: ABSOLUTELY NO human presence: no skin, no neck, no hands, no shoulders, no body underneath the fabric. Nothing but cloth.
blocks.flatlay_setup: flat-lay product photography, no person and no mannequin anywhere in the frame. The {{category.garment_noun_short}} is laid flat and face-up on {{campaign.flatlay_surface}} and photographed from directly above
